text: Theorem. Let \(Q\) be a finite \(3\)-group of class \(\le4\) such that (H1) \(\gamma_4(Q)\) has exponent dividing \(3\), and (H2) \(a^9\in\gamma_4(Q)\) for every \(a\in\gamma_2(Q)\). Then \(D_5(Q)=1\). More generally, \(D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)\) for every group \(G\) such that \(G/\gamma_2(G)\) is a finite \(3\)-group, \(\gamma_4(G)^3\subseteq\gamma_5(G)\) and \(\gamma_2(G)^9\subseteq\gamma_4(G)\).

Theorem 6.9 is the special case in which \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) has exponent \(\le3\): then \(\gamma_3/\gamma_4\) and \(\gamma_4\) are elementary abelian (identity (i) of its proof), so \(\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_3^3\subseteq\gamma_4\) and \(\gamma_4^3=1\). What is new is that \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) and \(\gamma_3/\gamma_4\) may have exponent \(9\). That these factors are elementary is not needed at all: instead of the cube map \(\pi\colon\gamma_2/\gamma_3\to\gamma_3/\gamma_4\), the rows (B) and (E) of Tahara's conditions are combined into a single identity \((\ast)\) in \(\gamma_3\), which is then paired with \(x_i\).
